Triggers.value: A specific temperature on the skin
Beginning to feel detached or unreal

Memory.value: When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief
When I think about the frightening event I can sometimes smell things that I smelt when the frightening event happened.
When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred.

Negative Appraisals.value: My reactions since the event show that I am a lousy coper
Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore
Nothing good can happen to me anymore

vignette: Rohan, a 26-year-old South Asian male and editor by profession, still recalls the chill of the handcuffs on his wrists that fateful night when he was detained by the police. The memory of the event has become a festering wound, with every recollection opening it anew. When Rohan remembers the incident, overwhelming grief washes over him, transporting him back to the despair and helplessness he felt in those moments. The smell of sweat and metal wafts through his nostrils, an olfactory recall that instantly revives the terror. As he navigates his daily life, certain triggers threaten to plunge him into this maelstrom of emotions. A specific temperature on his skin can send a shiver down his spine, reminding him of the cold, unforgiving surface of the police station's floor. Being alone with women, too, fills him with an unshakeable unease, as if their presence might somehow summon the same feelings of vulnerability he experienced that night. These triggers have become so potent that Rohan has begun to believe his reactions since the event demonstrate that he is a lousy coper. The memories linger, and with each recollection, his body seems to reenact the posture it assumed during those hours: shoulders slumped, wrists bent in a futile attempt to break free. Rohan's negative appraisals have taken hold, convincing him that nothing good can happen to him anymore. He feels lost, as if life has been drained of its meaning. These bleak outlooks, in turn, intensify his memories of the event, making them even more vivid and debilitating. The grief he experiences upon recall now seems like proof that he is indeed a poor coper. This self-perception, in turn, heightens his sensitivity to triggers, making him increasingly wary of situations that might evoke those dreaded feelings. The dissociative feeling that often accompanies these memories has begun to seep into Rohan's daily interactions. He feels detached from the world around him, as if observing life through a haze. His work as an editor suffers as a result; he finds himself struggling to connect with the words on the page, his mind constantly drifting back to that fateful night. Rohan's marriage has also borne the brunt of his struggles. His wife, once a source of comfort and strength, now unwittingly triggers the same feelings of unease. Rohan feels guilty for pushing her away, but the fear of being overwhelmed by his emotions keeps him at arm's length. He is desperate to break this cycle, to find meaning in life again, but the grip of his negative appraisals seems too strong. As Rohan sits in therapy, he confesses that it was a recent incident at work – a harmless touch on the shoulder from a female colleague – that sent him spiraling into the abyss. The memory of the event came flooding back, and with it, all the attendant emotions: grief, helplessness, and despair. It is this realization that has brought Rohan to seek help; he hopes that by addressing these wounds, he might finally begin to heal and rediscover a sense of purpose in his life.
